questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator be more visible to other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake lights properly.

questions.question: What is usually in the center of a traffic lane?
questions.explanation: Oil drippings from cars create a strip in the center of lanes. In dry conditions, motorcycles can usually ride safely on this strip.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows a motorcycle. Remember that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take and when should it be done?

options.text: A few minutes once a month.
A few minutes before every ride.
Over an hour by a mechanic.
Over an hour only with a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes just a few minutes.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulatory signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. Follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down on slippery surfaces. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce head and neck injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most effective way to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Where should you ride under normal conditions?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane

questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane under normal conditions with no hazards. Move your position if road conditions change.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: Let the tailgater get in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Going faster only makes it more dangerous.

questions.question: Slippery surfaces make it hard to control a motorcycle. Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement is slippery. Loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates in the road are also slippery. Ride slowly and carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden movements. Watch for oily spots, shaded areas, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these areas may have less grip.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes smoothly and together to stop safely. Do not lock up either tire.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal plates. Dry pavement provides good grip.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always scan ahead and look for potential dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because they are rare.
Look ahead but do not look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always scan ahead and look for potential dangers.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead of you. This helps you see hazards early and react to them before you reach them.

questions.question: Which one is NOT protective clothing for riders?
questions.explanation: Wear protective gear: a sturdy jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that support your ankles, and gloves. A stocking cap is not protective gear.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have brakes in both front and rear.
Have three brakes: front, rear, and emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on only when it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. It makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: Stopping will be harder than normal.
You want to look at the scenery.
You want other drivers to cut you off.
You want to hide from the driver ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will be harder than normal.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space if your motorcycle needs more distance to stop. Do this on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: When you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Expect it to handle like your own bike.
Trust the owner checked the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Do all safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle just like you would on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and allow extra stopping distance.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain in minutes and starts to affect the person.
It takes a long time to feel alcohol's effects.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain in minutes and starts to affect the person.
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly without digestion. It reaches the brain in minutes. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: A benefit of regular motorcycle maintenance is:

options.text: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
Maintenance takes a lot of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle will run well for a long time.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained motorcycle will ride like new. Regular maintenance and inspections keep your bike running well.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Use both brakes when braking and avoid sudden moves.
